newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. gives conflicting reports on Goma airport.
newsitem.headline: U.N. gives conflicting reports on Goma airport.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said it heard Tutsi rebels captured Goma airport in eastern Zaire from army troops on Thursday but later reported conflicting information.
"We are still receiving contradictory information about the status of the airport," Panos Moumtzis, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees in Goma city, said by telephone.
"We have no independent way to check on the airport."
Moumtzis initially said the airport had been taken over and the information was confirmed from the Zairean side. But he later said Zairean sources told UNHCR it remained in Zairean army hands.
"There is no movement in town. It is completely deserted," said Moumtzis, adding aid workers remained inside their offices in the lakeside city after heavy fighting since Thursday morning.
A Reuters correspondent in the Rwandan border town of Gisenyi said he could see fighting around Goma airport, five km (three miles) from the city centre, after Moumtzis said it had fallen.
Steve Pratt, an official with CARE International, told Reuters aid agencies had been told to prepare for a partial or total evacuation from Goma by road to neighbouring Rwanda.
Pratt earlier on Thursday quoted the Zairean military as saying if necessary it would give up the airport to attackers.
